hero.title: Jensen Huang,
hero.lede: An individual with no office, standing on a chokepoint. He can't write or veto a rule; what he has is a company that controls the main supply of AI compute, and direct access to the people who decide where it may be sold.

short_answer.title: Responses are fast and in person
short_answer.body: He answers a restriction within days: a trip to the capital that holds the gate, or public criticism.

short_answer.title: Few patterns yet
short_answer.body: One reaction (R2) is a pattern, with three independent cases. The rest rest on one or two and stay signals until new events test them.

purpose.summary: What Jensen says and does is in his control, so a persona built from his record can forecast it. It can't forecast events nobody controls.
use_for: When the US or China restricts chip sales, what does Jensen say, where does he go, and how fast?
Which proposed AI laws will he oppose, and in what terms?
After a safety incident is public, does he call for rules or reframe it?
Whom does he answer when criticised, and does his position move?
dont_use_for: Whether an incident happens at all, such as the July 2026 breach of Hugging Face by OpenAI's agents. The persona covers only his response once it is public.
NVIDIA's product and pricing decisions. Those belong to a company persona (see the attribution rule in step 2).

standing.class_role: Individual · founder and CEO of NVIDIA since 1993. No public office.
standing.principal: Answers to NVIDIA's board and shareholders. No row in the log shows the board overriding him, which is itself a gap (step 7).
standing.attribution_rule: A row counts as Jensen's when he did it in person (a trip, a meeting, a signature, a share sale) or when a reputable report names him as the one who announced or decided it. Anything else NVIDIA does is a context row: it can trigger his response but is not his act.
standing.veto_players: Commerce/BIS (licences), the President (deals on top of licences), Congress (statute, such as the GAIN AI Act) and Beijing (CAC and purchase guidance). Each can block a sale he wants.
standing.gates_held: Supply to partners: he told Supermicro to tighten compliance after a smuggling case (J32). His share sales run under a pre-set plan (J13).

gates.held_by: Commerce/BIS, with deals set by the President
gates.response: Lobbies in person (J16, J21), criticises in public (J10, J18, J22), restarts supply when cleared (J28)
Closed-door meetings with senators (J21); public attack on the GAIN AI Act (J22)

gates.gate: Permission for Chinese firms to buy
gates.response: Goes to China and praises its tech (J06, J15, J26); says he is disappointed (J17)
Demands compliance (J32): he holds this gate

gates.gate: Who joins a presidential trip or accord
gates.response: Goes when called (J30); signs when invited (J42)

limits.title: All rows secondary
limits.body: Every row rests on a report by an established outlet; none has been checked against the original transcript, video or filing.

limits.title: Personal records not pulled
limits.body: FEC donations, SEC Form 4 filings and foundation filings haven't been searched directly. The only personal financial row (J13) comes from a CNBC report of a Form 4.

limits.title: One coder
limits.body: Topics, stances and audiences were coded by one person (P6 not done). Stance on conditional statements (J40) is the most disputable.

limits.title: Board and private channels
limits.body: Nothing in the log shows the board constraining him, and most of his contact with Trump is private. Private lobbying is under-recorded.

limits.title: No baseline forecaster
limits.body: A fair baseline would predict from base rates alone, such as the median response gap. Without one, a fit shows the persona is consistent with events, not that it forecasts better.

rules.name: Restriction → public criticism
rules.when: A US restriction or a Chinese purchase block cuts NVIDIA's China sales
rules.then: Jensen criticises the policy in public, framed as handing the market to China or Huawei
rules.note: Two independent episodes in 2025, both under Trump (the GAIN Act being dropped, C09, was an easing and is not counted). The 2023 episode under Biden went the other way: he promised compliance. The reaction may depend on who holds the White House, which three episodes can't separate. Held out: no new restriction after the cutoff, so no test yet.

rules.name: Trump invites → Jensen goes
rules.when: Trump invites him to a trip, meeting or signing
rules.then: He goes, including at short notice
rules.note: One computable episode: the May 2026 delegation (C14 is his being left off, then called back). J09 and J42 have no invitation row, so they cannot count. The reaction predicts attendance, not policy.

rules.name: Restriction public → trip to China
rules.when: A restriction on China sales becomes public
rules.then: He travels to China within 2-10 days
rules.note: Two day-precise episodes. Confounded: J26 and J02 are also his annual Lunar New Year trip. Needs a restriction that lands away from late January.

rules.name: Safety alarm → reframe, not rules
rules.when: A public safety incident or warning
rules.then: Within 0-12 days he reframes it as an engineering, open-model or commercial question, not a reason for law
rules.note: Two independent waves (the July 2026 breach and the September 2026 disclosures), both after the cutoff, so built from held-out rows. The platform launch (K64) is NVIDIA’s act, not his. C16 is dated only to the week and is not counted.

rules.name: Off-message remark → same-day reframing
rules.when: A remark breaks the 'America must win' line
rules.then: He reframes it the same day around US leadership
rules.note: One episode. Watch for a second.

rules.name: Restriction → compliant product
rules.then: A chip designed to fit just under the limit
rules.note: This is a company act (A800/H800, H20, RTX Pro 6000D). Under the attribution rule it belongs to the NVIDIA persona, where it is reaction N5.

reach.reading: No federal decision on China sales logged in the next 30 days.
H20 licences assured five days after the meeting.
15% revenue-share deal announced five days later.
H200 sales cleared with a 25% cut five days later. The GAIN AI Act was dropped the same day (C09), so its order relative to the meeting is unknown.
20+ firms co-signed the letter he shared; they acted with him, not after him.

tests.note: No new US restriction or Chinese purchase block after the cutoff.
He signed the White House accord at Trump's lunch on 29 Sep 2026 (J42).
No new restriction after the cutoff.
Built from held-out rows (C15, C16, C27), so the rows can't also test it. Needs the next incident.

Framing AI as an existential threat
profile.decision_style: Commercial and pragmatic. Builds relationships with whoever holds power. When a remark causes trouble, he walks it back quickly (J19 → J20).

relations.note: Decides deals on top of licences and who travels with him
Licenses what NVIDIA may ship to China
Decides whether Chinese firms may buy
Public disagreement on jobs and safety

voice.summary: Engineer’s framing, upbeat, big numbers. Calls AI risk talk a “doomer narrative”.

say_do.say: America must win the AI race
say_do.do: Lobbies to sell advanced chips to China
